title: How do ten thousand years compare with the Earth?
description: Using the final scheme of leap years, the video counts the calendar days in ten thousand years, finds the Earth's days for ten thousand trips, and finds the difference and a way to fix it.
teaching_notes: One idea: sort the years into four kinds by what divides them, count the days, and compare with the Earth. Watch for children who count the century years as leap years.

source: With this final scheme of leap years can you calculate the number of calendar days in 10,000 years and the number of actual days the Earth will take to make 10,000 revolutions around the Sun? What is the difference? If there is a big difference, can you suggest a way to fix this problem?
video_script.why: The child has counted the days in a thousand calendar years with the final scheme of leap years, and now does the same for ten thousand years and looks for a fix.
video_script.substitution: the book's own ten thousand calendar years with the final scheme of leap years, against ten thousand trips of the Earth
video_script.anchor: Ten thousand calendar years with the final scheme of leap years, against ten thousand trips of the Earth
video_script.payoff_line: The two totals of days are now known.

final_answer.value: 3652425 calendar days against 3652422; the calendar is 3 days ahead; dropping about 3 leap days every 10000 years could fix it
final_answer.spoken: three million six hundred and fifty two thousand four hundred and twenty five calendar days against three million six hundred and fifty two thousand four hundred and twenty two; the calendar is three days ahead; dropping about three leap days in every ten thousand years could fix it

maths_rules: divisible by 400: 10000 ÷ 400 gives 25 years, each 366 days
divisible by 100 but not by 400: 100 − 25 = 75 years, each 365 days
divisible by 4 but not by 100: 2500 − 100 = 2400 years, each 366 days
size check: a thousand years had 365242 days, so ten thousand years have about 3650000 days
3652425 − 3652422 = 3, so the calendar is 3 days ahead
a fix: drop about 3 leap days in every 10000 years; check 3652425 − 3 = 3652422
video_script.design: One idea: sort the years into four kinds, count the days, compare with the Earth, and fix the gap. Assumes the video on a thousand years. The calendar total of three million six hundred and fifty two thousand four hundred and twenty five stays hidden until the answer beat and appears before that only as a sum of two products.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, count the years of each kind, as for a thousand years.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Ten thousand divided by four hundred gives twenty five.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Ten thousand divided by one hundred gives one hundred, so seventy five are not divisible by four hundred.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Ten thousand divided by four gives two thousand five hundred. Take away one hundred, and two thousand four hundred remain.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>The rest are ten thousand take away two thousand five hundred, which is seven thousand five hundred.
